target="_blank" >Fran Spielman</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydlrsud-l-o/" target="_blank" >Michael Puente</a></h5><p><b>Calls for reform</b>: A macabre discovery in a South Deering funeral home is once again revealing gaps in government oversight of facilities like South Chicago Chapel, where authorities found 56 decomposing bodies and 56 boxes of cremated remains, according to lawmakers now calling for state-level reform.</p><p><b>Key context</b>: Clark and Johanna Morgan, operators of South Chicago Chapel, are accused of mishandling the remains of more than 100 people. The Morgans also ran a Chicago Heights crematory that was shut down by the state last year for mishandling the remains of about 100 other people.</p><p><b>Who's responsible?</b> After the Morgans' Chicago Heights crematory closed, a new state law expanded the regulatory authority of the Illinois comptroller's office, which oversees crematories. But Comptroller Susana Mendoza's office doesn't regulate funeral directors or embalmers, who are licensed by the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation under Gov. JB Pritzker's administration.</p><p><b>'Bad actors' blamed</b>: Apparently, no state agency oversees funeral homes themselves, at their physical locations, officials said. At an unrelated event Monday, Pritzker said, "the comptroller's office did what they should do with the crematory. IDFPR did what it is supposed to do with regard to a funeral home and funeral directors, and so those, I think, seemingly were handled properly. ... >Kaitlin Washburn</a></h5><p><b>Family sues</b>: A Chicago police officer was in a "reckless and uncontrolled state of mind" when he fatally shot Derek Jordan earlier this year in Humboldt Park, his href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydlrsud-l-td/" target="_blank" >‘Cat tour’ brings a day of whimsy to Lincoln Square</a></h3><p></p><h5>Reporting by <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydlrsud-l-th/" target="_blank" >Erica Thompson</a></h5><p>On Saturday, a large crowd formed in Lincoln Square for an inaugural social gathering.</p><p>Among them was Nox, a sweet, shy Pisces who loves cuddles. There was also Diane, a fierce Tennessee native who loves long naps and cleanliness. No, they weren’t two singles at a dating event but two felines on the Lincoln Square Cat Tour.</p><p>For two hours, attendees hopped from house to house to view more than 125 residents’ cats on porches, or in windows and yards. They wore cat ears and cat patterns on their clothes. They carried cat-themed posters and cardboard cut-outs. One participant rolled her own cat in a stroller. Some used the official Google Map to go rogue, while others joined one of four guided routes with relevant names: Chonk, Zoomies, Primordial Pouch and Toe Beans.</p><p>More than 60 people, including some from out of state, showed up for the Chonk course.</p><p>From Minneapolis to Toronto, cat tours have become an international phenomenon, but the Lincoln Square soiree on Saturday — branded "Caturday" — was the first of its kind in Chicago. Organizers and attendees said they relished the opportunity to not only build community with their neighbors but be whimsical and escape the burdens of everyday life.</p><p>"This is a free, fun event that’s good for any age to get out there and do. It’s joyful, it’s silly, and I think people need it," said Christine Blevins, who helped organize the cat tour with her neighbor Kalin Webber.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydlrsud-l-tk/" target="_blank" ><b>READ MORE</b></a></p><hr><p></p><h4>YOUR DAILY QUESTION ☕️</h4><p><b>What's a book that changed the way you see Chicago? entries.title: Mayor Johnson wants City Council to impose moratorium on data centers
entries.summary: <p>Chicago should impose a temporary moratorium on new or expanded data centers until permanent regulations are established to mitigate their impact on the power grid, the water supply and the environment, Mayor Brandon Johnson said Tuesday in a move that an influential alderperson called a “political stunt.”</p><p>Johnson also signed an executive order establishing regulatory guardrails aimed at strengthening the city's approach toward data center development. </p><p></p><p>Two years ago, the City Council approved an ordinance championed by Zoning Committee Chair Gilbert Villegas (36th) that created a working group on data centers with input from affected city departments.</p><p>Preliminary recommendations on how to regulate the controversial industry have been released and were the focus of a recent hearing in the City Council’s Committee on Energy and Environmental Protection.</p><p>With those steps already taken, Villegas argued that Johnson’s executive order is unnecessary. Villegas said the mayor should merely introduce an ordinance that codifies the working group’s recommendations.</p><p>“This is just another political stunt by the mayor to say that he did something, given the fact that data centers right now are unpopular,” Villegas said Tuesday. “This is like the 100th executive order by this administration, instead of going through the regular ordinance process..." </p><p>Data centers have drawn fire in Chicago and across the country because of their potential to negatively affect the environment, drain water supplies and drive up energy costs. Johnson cited all of those potential negatives as he signed the executive order at Northerly Island, the nature park that once housed the lakefront airport known as Meigs Field.</p><p>Chicago is a "tech hub that embraces innovation, but never at the expense" of health, safety or the "natural environment," the mayor said. </p><p>"Chicagoans have been absolutely clear. They do not want data centers expanding across our city without strong protection for their communities, for their utility bills, for their air, water and their quality of life... We are answering their demands and centering our communities' concerns and solutions in our decision making," Johnson said. </p><p>"Before AI accelerates any faster, the city is taking steps now to protect Chicagoans from the impacts of data center development, while we undertake the comprehensive work that is necessary to establish permanent protections."</p><p>Chicago is the seventh largest market for data centers in the U.S., according to 2026 research by commercial real estate firm Avison Young. The city has been attractive, in part, because of its pro-business policies, including the 2024 ordinance that incentivized new data centers within city limits. But experts say new data centers in the region have increasingly been pushed to the south and west suburbs, where there’s more land for the large industrial buildings.</p><p>Nevertheless, pushback on data centers is growing, especially in suburbs like Grayslake and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/07/27/hawthorne-race-course-horse-track-buyer-data-center-developer-stickney-cicero-ai-artificial-intelligence" >Cicero.</a> Cicero trustees in July approved resolutions opposing a pair of rumored data centers, including one at the historic Hawthorne Race Course in neighboring Stickney.</p><p>The resolution opposing a data center at the former horse-racing track states that town officials don’t want any projects built anywhere near Cicero, home to more than 80,000 people.</p><p></p><p>There are currently 39 data centers within city limits, according to the city. The former Cboe headquarters downtown is still on track to be converted into a data center — and last week, the Commission on Chicago Landmarks’ Permit Review Committee approved plans to convert the lower floors of 300 W. Adams St. into a data center.</p><p>ComEd CEO Gil Quiniones told the Sun-Times in June there are around 100 proposed data center projects in Northern Illinois, though it’s unlikely that all will go forward. The centers have requested a combined 33 gigawatts of power from the utility.</p><p>“I think the sentiment [around data centers] has changed, and I believe that everyone is looking for — and we support it — more responsible development of data centers,” Quiniones said in the June interview. </p><p>The mayor was asked why he felt it necessary to issue yet another in a string of executive orders.</p><p></p><p>"We obviously have strong partnerships with City Council. What was important was to ensure that some of the vagueness around how environmental matters are addressed — that we clear that up," Johnson said. "Now there's absolute direction for departments to be able to do their part. That's the executive authority that I do have in this situation."</p><p> </p><p></p><p>Villegas said golf courses across the country gobble up 35 times the amount of water that data centers use, and that concerns about energy costs could have been addressed years ago if Johnson had negotiated a new franchise agreement with Commonwealth Edison.</p><p>“Data centers create a ton of property tax revenue that the city desperately needs and create hundreds of thousands of union jobs. But there is a balance here,” Villegas said. </p>

entries.title: Severe weather system leaves Chicago area amid airport delays, power outages
entries.summary: <p>A fast-moving storm system raced through multiple counties in the Chicago area, that included wind gusts as high as 99 miles per hour at the Gary, Indiana, airport and throughout many areas of the state </p><p>National Weather Service meteorologist Scott Baker said tornado teams were on their way to far southern Cook County and northern Will County to check for damage, but nothing has been confirmed. </p><p>Rainfall and damage totals are also not in yet, said Baker, who added the rainfall will probably range between 1 and 2 inches. </p><p>"So severe weather has moved out and the thunderstorm watch and tornado warnings are all gone by now," Baker said at 12:45 p.m. </p><p>A lakeshore flood advisory, including for the southern half of Cook County, does remain in effect until 5 p.m. </p><p>Earlier, the NWS said a severe thunderstorm watch would remains in effect until about 2 p.m.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Severe Thunderstorm Warning continues for Chicago IL, Cicero IL and Orland Park IL until 11:15 AM CDT. This storm will contain wind gusts to 70 MPH! <a href="https://t.co/QG0vUFJHQp">pic.twitter.com/QG0vUFJHQp</a></p>— NWS Chicago (@NWSChicago) <a href="https://x.com/NWSChicago/status/2087207354613785021?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 11, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>As of about noon, 289,633 ComEd customers, many of whom are in the south and southwest suburbs, were without power due to the storms, according to the utility company.</p><p>The storms also wreaked havoc on air travel.</p><p>As of about 12:25 p.m., delays were averaging 83 minutes at O'Hare with a total of 251 cancellations, according to <a class="Link" href="https://www.flychicago.com/business/media/delays/pages/default.aspx" target="_blank" >FlyChicago.com</a>. At Midway conditions were less severe, with delays averaging about 40 minutes, and only a handful of cancellations.</p><p>Those going to O’Hare have been recommended to check with their airlines for any flight-specific updates, as conditions change throughout the day.</p><p>18 total counties in Illinois were affected, including Cook County, with areas extending across northern and central portions of the state. Also including Livingston County in central Illinois; Ford and Iroquois counties in east-central Illinois; and Boone, DeKalb, La Salle, Lee, Ogle and Winnebago counties in north-central Illinois.</p><p>According to the NWS, the storm also impacted northwest Indiana and Wisconsin, affecting many communities near the I-74 corridor.</p><p>The weather service earlier urged residents to remain aware as the inclement weather moves through the region. </p><p>Along with the high winds, some areas potentially receiving around a quarter-inch or more of rainfall. Frequent lightning is also expected through the storm, with heavy downpours and flooding in certain areas being possible.<br></p>

entries.title: What to know about the 2026 Chicago Air and Water Show
entries.summary:
The roar of fighter jets will once again fill the skies over Lake Michigan this weekend, as Chicago’s annual Air and Water Show will return to the city this year — with another appearance from the U.S Air Force Thunderbirds.

How to watch the show

The free city-wide spectacle, which usually draws upwards of 1 million people every year, will run shows on Aug. 15 and 16, taking place from 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m. on both days. The show will stretch along the lakefront, beginning at Fullerton Avenue to Oak Street, with North Avenue beach serving as the center of the show.

What’s special about this year?

While the nation’s independence day was last month, the Air and Water Show will celebrate the nation's 250th birthday, said Mayor Brandon Johnson in a statement.

"The Chicago Air and Water Show is one of Chicago’s defining summer traditions, bringing families, visitors and aviation enthusiasts together along our extraordinary lakefront," Johnson said. "As our nation marks its 250th anniversary, we are proud to celebrate the spirit of innovation, service and patriotism that has inspired generations, while showcasing the very best our city has to offer."

American Airlines, who is the presenting sponsor of the event, will open each day with a ceremonial flyover. On Saturday, the flyover will feature a special Centennial livery aircraft, while Sunday’s will feature a America250 livery.

Who is flying?

In addition to the usual military and civilian performers, this year’s show will feature the return of the Thunderbirds for their second consecutive year. The Thunderbirds and U.S. Navy Blue Angels have historically traded off years appearing at the Chicago show, but the city said this year's break with tradition was due to a scheduling issue on the part of the Blue Angels.

For more information about the show, go to: chicagoairandwatershow.us.

What are the featured airplanes and performers?

Featured military performers:

  • U.S. Air Force C-17 Demo – 15th Airlift Squadron
  • Illinois Air National Guard KC-135 – 126th Air Refueling Wing
  • U.S. Coast Guard Search & Rescue Demo
  • F-22 Raptor Demonstration Team
  • USMC F-35B Lightning II Demonstration Team

Featured civilian performers:

  • Kevin Coleman – Red Bull
  • Susan Dacy Super Stearman “Big Red”
  • Ed Hamill Folds of Honor Biplane 
  • Trojan Phlyers Flight Demonstration Team
  • Chicago Police Department Helicopters
  • Chicago Fire Department Air / Sea Rescue

For those attending, public parking will not be available at North Avenue Beach. The city encourages visitors to take public transportation. Pick-up and drop-off will be available at the northbound entrance of DuSable Lake Shore Drive depending on crowd size. Spectators will also be able to watch from the sand or grass, with an accessible viewing area near Castaways.

What about sonic booms?

The Thunderbirds made headlines last year as, according to experts, their aircraft went supersonic.

During the 2025 show, many residents of Lake View reported feeling strong vibrations as the jets flew overhead, suspecting a sonic boom, as several windows were damaged across the 44th Ward.

The Air Force said the Thunderbirds did not go supersonic during the demonstration. But an aeronautics professor who reviewed video of the flights previously told the Sun-Times that the footage showed what were “clearly sonic booms,” which occurs when an aircraft exceeds the speed of sound.

An Air Force spokesperson did not respond immediately to a request for comment.

Contributing: Courtney Kueppers

entries.title: Man arrested at O'Hare accused in fatal Albany Park stabbing
entries.summary: <p>A man who was arrested at O'Hare International Airport apparently trying to board a flight is facing first-degree murder charges for stabbing a woman to death over the weekend in the Albany Park neighborhood, according to Chicago police and sources. </p><p>Ankur Patel, 31, is accused of stabbing a 32-year-old woman inside an apartment in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/09/woman-fatally-stabbed-albany-park" target="_blank" >4800 block of North Avers Avenue</a> around 1:45 a.m. Sunday, Chicago police said.</p><p>The woman, whose name hasn’t been released, was found unresponsive in the apartment hallway next to the bathroom, according to a police report obtained by the Chicago Sun-Times. She had been stabbed in her neck and was pronounced dead at the scene.</p><p>Patel was arrested while going through security at O'Hare Airport nine hours after the incident happened, according to police and sources.</p><p>Patel was scheduled to appear in court Tuesday.</p>

entries.title: Asesinan a tiros a dos conserjes en una escuela primaria en el suroeste de Chicago
entries.summary: <p>Dos conserjes fueron abatidos a tiros dentro de la Escuela Primaria Mark Twain, en el vecindario de Garfield Ridge, la tarde del lunes en lo que parece haber sido un homicidio-suicidio, según transmisiones preliminares de la radio policial.</p><p>Según un comunicado de la Policía de Chicago, un hombre de 63 años y una mujer de 48 fueron encontrados, cada uno, con una sola herida de bala en la cabeza dentro de la escuela ubicada en la cuadra 5100 al sur de Lotus Avenue a las 3:40 p.m.</p><p>Ambos fueron trasladados al Christ Medical Center, donde fueron declarados muertos, dijo la policía. En la escena se recuperó un arma, según añadieron.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-c90000" name="module-c90000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>De acuerdo con las transmisiones de la radio policial, una operadora dijo que el tiroteo se originó por una disputa entre dos conserjes. Ambas personas fueron halladas dentro de la Escuela Primaria Mark Twain, según los despachos de radio. Uno de ellos fue encontrado en la cafetería de la escuela, dijo la operadora.</p><p>Ambas víctimas de disparos eran conserjes, dijo Eric Bailey, portavoz de SEIU Local 73, que representa a los conserjes de las Escuelas Públicas de Chicago (CPS).</p><p>No había estudiantes en la escuela, ya que las clases no comienzan hasta el 24 de agosto.</p><p>Trumaine Reeves, vicepresidente ejecutivo de SEIU Local 73, dijo en un comunicado por correo electrónico que "los únicos hechos que conocemos ahora mismo son que dos familias han perdido a un ser querido y nuestras oraciones están con sus familias, y con el personal, los estudiantes y las familias de la Escuela Primaria Mark Twain".</p><p>Las Escuelas Públicas de Chicago no respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios.</p><p>Una vecina que vive frente a la escuela dijo al Sun-Times que vio cómo el personal de primeros auxilios sacó el cuerpo de un hombre y luego el de una mujer del interior de la escuela. La respuesta de emergencia incluyó inicialmente cuatro camiones de bomberos y cuatro ambulancias, según la mujer, que pidió no revelar su nombre.</p><p>La noche del lunes se vio a varios oficiales y detectives dentro y fuera de la escuela.</p><p>No se difundió información adicional de inmediato.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Motorist flees, causes multiple crashes in fatal Lake View hit-and-run
entries.summary: <p>A impaired motorist who fatally slammed into a 25-year-old pedestrian before fleeing, crashing into a vehicle causing a chain-reaction crash and another chase that ended when he plowed into a tree Saturday has been charged, police said. f</p><p>Miroslaw Ciszek, 34, was arrested Sunday and charged with one felony count of aggravated DUI causing accident or death and leaving the scene of an accident causing injury or death, Chicago police said. He was expected to appear for a detention hearing Tuesday. </p><p>About four hours earlier, Sarah Milcarek, 25, was walking between two parked cars in the 1400 block of Irving Park Road around 9:20 p.m. when Ciszek allegedly struck her with the car he was driving, police said. </p><p>Ciszek then allegedly fled west and crashed into an SUV, which then hit a black sedan. The driver of the SUV tried to detain him, but he got back into his car and fled again before crashing into a tree, according to police. </p><p>Ciszek then got out of the car and ran off, then entering a building in the 4000 block of North Ashland Avenue, police said.</p><p>Milcarek, of Missiouri, was taken to Advocate Illinois Masonic Medical Center where she was later pronounced dead, according to police.</p><p>Ciszek is expected to appear for a detention hearing Tuesday. </p>

entries.title: Breaking down the Bears' first depth chart of the preseason
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> haven’t picked a starting left tackle, officially or unofficially.</p><p>The team listed all three candidates as potential starters on the depth chart they released Tuesday. For what it’s worth, the order on the two-deep lines up with the amount of snaps each has taken with the first team — it reads “Braxton Jones OR Jedrick Wills Jr. OR Kiran Amegadjie.”</p><p>The Bears, of course, insist their two-deep is far from official. Rather, they’re required to post it in advance of Saturday’s preseason opener against the Browns at Soldier Field. Most of the Bears starters are unlikely to play much, if at all, on Saturday.</p><p>Dayo Odeyingbo is listed as the starting defensive end opposite Montez Sweat. He figures to bump inside on passing downs so Austin Booker can take his place at end.</p><p>Safety Coby Bryant, who will be out the next two months with a knee injury, is still listed as a starter, as is wide receiver Luther Burden, who will miss the rest of the preseason <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/10/bears-luther-burden-groin-injury-preseason-miss-nfl-wide-receiver-practice-tyrique-stevenson" target="_blank" >with a groin problem</a>. Players on the Physically Unable to Perform list, such as slot cornerback Kyler Gordon, aren't listed on the roster.</p><p>Below are the Bears’ listed starters:</p><h3>OFFENSE</h3><p>WR Rome Odunze<br>WR Luther Burden<br>LT Braxton Jones OR Jedrick Wills Jr. OR Kiran Amegadjie<br>LG Joe Thuney<br>C Garrett Bradbury<br>RG Jonah Jackson<br>RT Darnell Wright<br>TE Cole Kmet<br>TE Colston Loveland<br>QB Caleb Williams<br>RB D’Andre Swift</p><h3>DEFENSE</h3><p>DE Montez Sweat<br>DT Grady Jarrett<br>DT Gervon Dexter<br>DE Dayo Odeyingbo<br>LB TJ Edwards<br>LB Devin Bush<br>CB Tyrique Stevenson<br>CB Jaylon Johnson<br>DB Cam Lewis<br>S Coby Bryant<br>S Dillon Thieneman</p><h3>SPECIAL TEAMS</h3><p>K Cairo Santos<br>P Tory Taylor<br>HOLDER Tory Taylor<br>LS Beau Gardner<br>KR Kalif Raymond<br>PR Kalif Raymond</p>

entries.title: Trump signs executive order calling for spacing out childhood shots
entries.summary: <p>NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump on Monday signed an executive order calling for revamped <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/childhood-vaccine-schedule-trump-rfk-hhs-d04ba53d6820cc7194a4885e2418d132" target="_blank" >childhood vaccine recommendations</a> that promote his long-held belief that childhood shots should be spaced out into separate medical visits.</p><p>The order recommends separating the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine into three different shots administered in separate visits, and directs the nation’s health department to improve vaccine research, says a White House fact sheet, first reported by The Daily Caller. Separate measles, mumps and rubella vaccines for children are not currently available in the United States.</p><p>Speaking about the order at the Oval Office on Monday, Trump also said that one-year-olds should have their shots separated out into five separate visits, though it wasn’t clear whether he was talking about all the vaccines they receive or specific ones.</p><p>Public health experts have raised concerns that spacing out shots as Trump suggests can lead to an increased risk that children become infected with a vaccine-preventable disease before returning for another visit. Childhood vaccines — and how and when to give them in combination — go through rigorous studies, and safety tracking continues for years as the shots are used.</p><p>Even as the order calls for revised vaccine recommendations, states, not the federal government, have the authority to require vaccinations for schoolchildren. The order will advise states with school vaccine mandates to consider updating their laws to reflect the administration’s recommendations, the fact sheet said.</p><p>On Tuesday, the Illinois Department of Public Health reaffirmed that the state's guidelines will still follow recommendations from the <a class="Link" href="https://publications.aap.org/redbook/resources/15585/AAP-Immunization-Schedule" target="_blank" >American Academy of Pediatrics</a>. Those guidelines, for example, still include multiple doses for infants to be vaccinated against hepatitis B. It also still calls for the combined vaccine that protects young children from measles, mumps and rubella.</p><p>Dr. Sameer Vohra, the director of IDPH, said Trump's executive order is not supported by scientific evidence and will create a greater burden for parents. He added that state health officials will ensure residents have access to vaccines. </p><p>"IDPH will continue to be guided by science and work closely with clinical and community leaders to provide recommendations that allow Illinoisians to make the best choices to keep themselves and their families safe and healthy," Vohra said in a prepared statement. </p><p>Last year, Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker signed into law a measure that called for the state to create its own <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2025/12/05/cdc-vaccine-newborns-hepatitis-b-robert-kennedy-anti-vaccine-childhood" target="_blank" >vaccine guidelines</a> and it requires state-regulated health insurance plans to cover the vaccinations. </p><p></p><p>Last December, Trump ordered the federal Department of Health and Human Services to review how peer nations approach vaccine recommendations and consider revising U.S. guidance accordingly. The department responded by cutting the number of <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/rfk-jr-vaccine-trump-science-autism-9b99621b01f11b7f0bdc81e5a0b82d2b" target="_blank" >vaccines</a> it recommends for every child, a move that has since been blocked in court.</p><p>In the months leading up to Monday’s announcement, Trump’s administration had largely pivoted away from talking about vaccine policy in favor of less polarizing topics like healthy eating and efforts to lower drug prices ahead of November’s elections. Polls show most Americans <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/vaccines-childhood-vaccinations-vaccine-mandate-kennedy-521201a8e4100f3cc1a8f1f5a7423b77" target="_blank" >still support school vaccine requirements</a>, though Republicans are less likely than Democrats to see them as important.</p><p>Still, Trump has been fixated on connecting autism to vaccines. He has recently ramped up pressure on Secretary Kennedy to identify the cause of autism, something Kennedy had pledged to do with new research unveiled last year. Trump publicly prodded the health secretary for an update on autism research in a Cabinet meeting last month.</p><p>“How are you doing on the autism research?” Trump asked.</p><p>“We will have an answer for you,” Kennedy said.</p><p>Scientific consensus and decades of studies have firmly concluded there is no link between childhood vaccines and autism. On Monday, Kennedy repeated his assertion that he believes an unknown environmental factor is to blame for rising autism diagnoses and said that his department will deliver research findings “as soon as they are ready.”</p><p>The order comes as school years are starting around the country and the nation contends with a measles outbreak that experts say could result in the U.S. losing its <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/us-measles-elimination-mexico-6f0bc8f7ef31d5ef82492e42ccb38e47" target="_blank" >measles elimination status</a>.</p><p>On Monday, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2026/08/10/american-academy-of-pediatrics-flu-vaccine-recommendation-kids-6-months-older-health" target="_blank" >American Academy of Pediatrics </a>issued its own report analyzing the safety of this year's flu vaccine, and determined it was safe for children aged 6 months and older. It recommended all children older than 6 months get the vaccine this season. </p>

entries.title: Bears LT Ozzy Trapilo ahead of schedule in recovery from knee injury, could practice before season starts
entries.summary: <p>Injury news usually is bad, but <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a> had a surprisingly optimistic update on left tackle Ozzy Trapilo on Tuesday.</p><p>Trapilo ruptured the patellar tendon in his knee during the playoffs, and the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/01/21/bears-list-of-injury-concerns-grows-late-in-season-starting-with-lt-ozzy-trapilo" >Bears prepared for the possibility he’d miss the entire upcoming season</a>. However, Trapilo has been ahead of schedule in his recovery, and coach Ben Johnson said Tuesday it’s possible he’ll be able to practice before the season starts.</p><p>“We’ll see how things go, but he’s doing a good job working right now,” Johnson said. “He’s been attacking this thing head on. He’s been here pretty much all summer. I’ve gotten to see him every single day, and he’s doing a great job with the rehab process.</p><p>“There’s still a lot of things that he’s got to hit in terms of making himself available for practice, but he’s done a really nice job with the rehab.”</p><p>Trapilo was a second-round pick last year and took over the starting job in Week 12 against the Steelers. He held it until suffering the knee injury in the playoff win over the Packers.</p><p>While the Bears didn’t use a high draft pick or spend big in free agency to replace him, they did move forward with Braxton Jones as the presumptive left tackle. Jones has been leading the competition over Jedrick Wills, Theo Benedet and Kiran Amegadjie.</p><p>Jones has been out with a minor injury, but is expected back on the field soon, and Johnson said the team could decide on a left tackle when the coaching staff meets Wednesday.</p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" entries.title: Bears S Coby Bryant undergoes knee surgery, now out until at least December
entries.summary: <p>When <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> safety Coby Bryant got hurt last week, the team believed he’d still be back by October. Upon further medical examination, it’s now possible he’ll miss the season.</p><p>Byrant initially was diagnosed with a hyperextension, bone bruise and small fracture in his left knee. He had surgery Friday, and coach Ben Johnson said Tuesday his timeline to return is 4-6 months.</p><p>The best-case scenario there would be him rejoining the team late in the regular season, while back end of that projection would be around the Super Bowl.</p><p>"He's going to be in a hurry to get back to help us out there at the end of the year," Johnson said.</p><p>Bryant, 27, was the Bears’ biggest offseason acquisition. He came from the defending champion Seahawks and got a three-year, $40 million contract at a time when the Bears were shedding money to get under the salary cap.</p><p>They expected him to be a pillar of their defense and mentor first-round pick <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/04/24/dillon-thieneman-got-to-the-nfl-by-using-criticism-to-improve-thatll-serve-him-well-with-the-bears" >Dillon Thieneman</a> during his rookie season. The Bears likely will go with Cam Lewis, who has played cornerback and safety, in Bryant’s spot, though he’s been out recently with a minor injury.</p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module entries.title: Pediatras a nivel nacional dicen que todos los niños de 6 meses en adelante deben vacunarse contra la gripe
entries.summary: <p>La Academia Estadounidense de Pediatría (AAP) insta a que los niños de 6 meses en adelante reciban la vacuna contra la gripe de este año. La organización, con sede en Illinois, hace la recomendación antes de que cualquier agencia federal publique sus propias directrices para la próxima temporada de gripe.</p><p>El año pasado, los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) retiraron su recomendación universal de mucho tiempo sobre la vacuna anual contra la gripe del calendario de vacunación infantil. En su lugar, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2026/01/05/us-drops-the-number-of-vaccines-it-recommends-for-every-child" target="_blank" >los CDC sólo dijeron</a> que ciertos grupos "de alto riesgo" necesitan vacunarse o hacerlo cuando los médicos lo recomiendan, en lo que se denomina como una "toma de decisiones compartida".</p><p>En un comunicado, la organización pediátrica subrayó la seguridad y los beneficios de la vacuna, especialmente después de que casi 200 niños murieron por la gripe durante la temporada 2025-2026. Menos del 50% de los niños de 6 meses a 17 años fueron vacunados, según el grupo.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-2e0000" name="module-2e0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>"Las buenas noticias son que las vacunas contra la gripe se han estudiado a fondo", dijo la Dra. Kristina Bryant, miembro del comité de enfermedades infecciosas de la Academia Estadounidense de Pediatría.</p><p>"Sabemos que son seguras para los niños y que pueden prevenir no sólo hospitalizaciones y muertes, sino que cada año evitan una cantidad considerable de enfermedades que terminan en visitas al consultorio médico", destacó Bryant en un comunicado. "Queremos mantener a los niños sanos y en la escuela, y a los padres sanos y en el trabajo. Las vacunas contra la gripe pueden ayudarnos a lograr eso".</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://publications.aap.org/pediatrics/article-abstract/158/2/e2026076453/208191/Influenza-Vaccine-Effectiveness-Against-Pediatric?redirectedFrom=fulltext" target="_blank" >Un estudio reciente de los CDC</a> reveló que la vacuna contra la gripe reduce en un 80% el riesgo de que niños y adolescentes mueran por el virus. Durante la temporada 2024-2025, <a class="Link" href="https://www.cdc.gov/flu-burden/php/data-vis-vac/index.html" target="_blank" >los CDC estiman</a> que la vacuna previno casi 15,000 hospitalizaciones y 245 muertes en niños y adolescentes.</p><p>La Academia Estadounidense de Pediatría señaló que los CDC aún no han publicado nuevas recomendaciones sobre la vacuna contra la gripe.</p><p>El grupo de pediatría recomienda que los niños reciban la vacuna tan pronto como esté disponible, idealmente antes de fines de octubre, antes del inicio de la temporada de gripe. También se anima a las mujeres embarazadas y a las que amamantan a vacunarse para protegerse a sí mismas y a sus bebés.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2025/09/10/covid-19-vaccines-arrive-at-chicago-pharmacies-as-pediatricians-wait-for-doses-and-guidance" target="_blank" >Los pediatras le dijeron anteriormente al Sun-Times</a> que lo mejor para todos es ponerse la vacuna contra la gripe justo antes del invierno, porque la vacuna funciona mejor entre las ocho y las 12 semanas posteriores a su aplicación.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: Marimar Martínez y otros denuncian a agentes del Operativo Midway Blitz buscando rendición de cuentas
entries.summary: <p>Casi un año después de que el presidente Donald Trump lanzara su campaña de deportaciones por toda el área de Chicago, un grupo de residentes inició el lunes un nuevo esfuerzo para responsabilizar a los agentes federales por presuntos delitos, presentando denuncias policiales y exigiendo investigaciones.</p><p>Entre ellos está <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/02/04/marimar-martinez-baleada-por-agentes-de-migracion-se-pronuncia-contra-asesinatos" target="_blank" >Marimar Martínez</a>, la mujer a la que el agente de la Patrulla Fronteriza, Charles Exum, le disparó cinco veces en octubre pasado. A pesar de indicios iniciales de una investigación federal sobre las circunstancias de su tiroteo, Martínez dijo que no ha sido entrevistada por los agentes federales en los 10 meses transcurridos desde entonces.</p><p>Así que por primera vez el lunes, Martínez pidió en cambio a las autoridades estatales y locales que actúen. Lo hizo al unirse a ocho personas más que marcharon hasta la sede del Área 3 del Departamento de Policía de Chicago en North Center para denunciar los presuntos delitos de los federales.</p><p>“Hoy exijo que nuestras autoridades locales y estatales hagan su trabajo y protejan a sus ciudadanos de estas conductas criminales que [Inmigración y el Control de Aduanas] y la Patrulla Fronteriza han infligido a sus víctimas”, dijo Martínez.</p><p>Ningún agente federal ha sido acusado de un delito en servicio relacionado con el Operativo Midway Blitz, a pesar de las amplias llamadas a la rendición de cuentas. La jueza de circuito del Condado de Cook, Erica Reddick, en mayo <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/05/26/jueza-del-condado-de-cook-rechaza-nombrar-fiscal-especial-para-investigar-agentes-de-operativo-midway-blitz" target="_blank" >negó una solicitud de un fiscal especial</a> que podría haber investigado a los agentes, tras preguntar si alguien había presentado realmente una denuncia policial.</p><p>“Hoy respondemos a esa preocupación”, dijo Berto Aguayo, abogado y organizador comunitario, quien asegura que él y otros fueron rociados indiscriminadamente con gas lacrimógeno por agentes federales.</p><p>“Cuando la gente común tiene el coraje de hacer su trabajo como ciudadanos, esperamos que las personas encargadas de hacer cumplir nuestras leyes hagan el suyo”, comentó Aguayo. “Así que hoy tenemos tres palabras para la Fiscal del Condado de Cook y cualquier otro organismo investigador: hagan su trabajo”.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" </div><p></p><p>La oficina de la Fiscal del Condado de Cook, Eileen O’Neill Burke, ha subrayado que es responsabilidad de agencias de cumplimiento de la ley como el Departamento de Policía de Chicago (CPD) investigar y construir un caso contra los agentes acusados de violar la ley antes de que su oficina pueda presentar cargos.</p><p>Eso convierte la “presentación masiva” de denuncias del lunes en un posible paso clave para ese fin, especialmente dada la pregunta planteada por Reddick. Un portavoz de CPD dijo el lunes que cada denuncia “será revisada para determinar si existió una violación de la ley local o estatal”.</p><p>Mientras tanto, la oficina de O’Neill Burke formó en julio un nuevo grupo de trabajo para ayudar a guiar y apoyar ese tipo de investigaciones —incluyendo evaluar si procede presentar cargos criminales. Su oficina también <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/02/19/chicago-ice-crime-border-patrol-trump-midway-blitz-alex-pretti-renee-good-eileen-oneill-burke" target="_blank" >publicó un protocolo para la presentación de cargos</a> a principios de año.</p><p>“Nadie está por encima de la ley —incluyendo los agentes federales— y la [Oficina de la Fiscal del Estado del Condado de Cook] no dudará en procesar cualquier caso cuando esté respaldado por la evidencia y la ley”, dijo la oficina de Burke en un comunicado.</p><p>La comisionada del Condado de Cook, Jessica Vásquez, ayudó a organizar la presentación del lunes. Dijo que todos los que denunciaron un delito contaban con su propio abogado y con pruebas para presentar ante la policía. También prometió que el acto del lunes no sería el último.</p><p>Brian Orozco, abogado que ayudó a muchos clientes el lunes, dijo que los presuntos delitos iban desde detención ilegal hasta agresión física e intento de homicidio.</p><p>Jimmy Arce, de la Illinois Accountability Commission, también reconoció “una voz muy importante que no pudo hablar con nosotros porque su vida fue truncada”. Era una referencia a Silverio Villegas González, un padre que fue asesinado a tiros por agentes de ICE en Franklin Park el pasado septiembre.</p><p>En abril, la Policía Estatal de Illinois <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/05/06/policia-del-estado-de-illinois-inicia-investigacion-sobre-tiroteo-mortal-de-silverio-villegas-gonzalez-por-ice" target="_blank" >abrió una investigación</a> sobre la muerte de Villegas González.</p><p>Otros han intentado —y fracasado— notificar a la policía local. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/07/29/residente-de-lake-view-demanda-al-gobierno-federal-por-allanar-su-casa-y-detener-a-trabajador-durante-operativo" target="_blank" >Leo Feler</a>, un hombre de Lake View que asegura que agentes entraron ilegalmente en su casa para perseguir a trabajadores de construcción, dijo que intentó dos veces presentar denuncias en una estación de policía de Chicago.</p><p>La primera vez lo rechazaron. La segunda vez, dijo, un oficial presentó un reporte de policía por daño criminal a la propiedad, pero más tarde recibió una llamada de un sargento informándole que no seguirían adelante con el caso.</p><p>No fue hasta <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/07/22/policia-de-chicago-establece-guias-para-recopilar-pruebas-de-agentes-de-ice-sospechosos-de-violar-la-ley" target="_blank" >el mes pasado</a> que el CPD emitió finalmente directrices formales sobre cómo tratar las quejas contra agentes federales.</p><p>La guía llegó tras la indignación pública porque el departamento no estaba cumpliendo una orden ejecutiva municipal de seis meses que exigía al departamento desarrollar procedimientos formales para recibir quejas y recopilar pruebas contra agentes federales sospechosos de infringir la ley.</p><p>Las nuevas directrices exigen que los oficiales notifiquen a sus supervisores de una denuncia y llenen un reporte informativo identificando al agente o agencia federal involucrada, así como la información de testigos y denunciantes. Los oficiales deben entregar al denunciante un número de informe.</p><p>Además, las denuncias pueden escalarse tras la revisión de los supervisores. Por ejemplo, si el incidente involucró una muerte, un tiroteo u otro acto de violencia, el caso sería remitido a la policía judicial del CPD y luego, potencialmente, a la oficina de la Fiscal del Condado de Cook.</p><p>La oficina de O’Neill Burke formó en julio un nuevo grupo de trabajo para abordar el tipo de investigaciones que buscaban Martinez y otros el lunes.</p><p>Conocido como el Federal Enforcement Action Felony Review Group, está destinado a ayudar en “asuntos que involucren actividad de aplicación de la ley federal en servicio, incluyendo acciones de control migratorio, conducta relacionada con el derecho a votar y actividad electoral, y cualquier otra mala conducta perpetrada por agentes federales que sea potencialmente de índole criminal”, según la oficina de Burke.</p><p>Se espera que incluya miembros de las unidades de revisión de delitos graves y de gran jurado de la oficina de Burke, entre otros, con preferencia por personal con experiencia en cortes federales.</p><p>Si bien la oficina de O’Neill Burke debe aprobar cualquier cargo por delito grave, las fuerzas del orden locales tienen la facultad de decidir de forma independiente sobre cargos por delitos menores.</p><p>La visita de Martínez al interior de la jefatura del Área 3 duró aproximadamente dos horas. Más tarde dijo que a los oficiales les tomó al menos media hora tomarles la declaración. Una vez fuera, dijo que se había sentido bien con la experiencia.</p><p>“Después de 10 meses, he estado esperando esto”, dijo Martínez. “En realidad, he estado esperando a que esto saliera a la luz y a hablar. Es hora. El cambio empieza con nosotros”.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" >La Voz Chicago</a></p>

entries.title: No timeline for a decision on Tony Romo's future, CBS Sports president says
entries.summary: <p>NEW YORK — CBS Sports president David Berson said Tuesday he does not have a timeline for a decision about Tony Romo's future.</p><p>Romo, the network's lead NFL analyst, is on leave <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports-media/2026/07/31/cbs-puts-tony-romo-on-leave-after-arrest-on-suspicion-of-operating-vehicle-under-the-influence" >following his arrest last month</a> in Wisconsin on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence.</p><p>"It's an evolving situation, and therefore we're still assessing," Berson said during a network event.</p><p>Berson also told reporters the decision to place Romo on indefinite leave was intended to shift attention toward the games and away from his legal situation.</p><p>"We we had to consider the impact on our image and on our brand. That's very important to us. Whether the games, marketing, PR, social, the focus should and needs to be on our presentation and not on any other factors," he said.</p><p>Analyst JJ Watt will join play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson on CBS Sports' lead NFL team during Romo's absence. Their first game will be on Sept. 13, when the Minnesota Vikings host the Green Bay Packers.</p><p>Watt joined CBS in 2023. He was an analyst on "The NFL Today" for two seasons before teaming with Ian Eagle on the network's No. 2 crew beginning last season. Ross Tucker has been moved up to the No. 2 team. He has previously teamed with Eagle on radio broadcasts for Westwood One.</p><p>Romo, 46, has been the lead game analyst for CBS' NFL coverage since 2017 after making four Pro Bowl appearances during a playing career that ran from 2004-16 and was spent entirely with Dallas.</p><p>He was arrested July 23 after he was stopped while driving south on Interstate 43 in Wisconsin. According to the Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office, Romo performed poorly on field sobriety tests before getting arrested, booked and released.</p><p>He has a court date set for Sept. 21.</p><p>Romo went to high school about 35 miles southwest of Milwaukee in Burlington, Wisconsin.<br></p>

entries.title: Catcher Drew Romo sticking with White Sox because of his preparation, work with pitchers
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> have been forced to make several changes at catcher because of injuries this season, but since being called up April 25, Drew Romo hasn’t been one of them.</p><p>Fans look at his .126 batting average entering Tuesday and wonder why. So an intrepid reporter asked Romo, as politely as possible, what makes him good, like …</p><p>“Why am I here?” he replied.</p><p>That certainly didn’t sound polite, but since he brought it up, yeah. What would you say you do here?</p><p>“I would say most important is I’ve done a great job with the pitchers,” Romo said. “I really learned from my past few years in professional baseball [with] scouting reports, attacking hitters, pitch sequencing, game-planning, being able to have clear communication with the coaching staff, pitchers, teammates.”</p><p>But he knows what fans see.</p><p>“Obviously, I’m not hitting good right now,” he said. “But right now I care more about winning games and after that my pitchers’ ERAs and not giving up runs. That to me is most important.”</p><p>The Sox claimed Romo, 24, off waivers from the Mets in January and sent him to Triple-A Charlotte. After beginning the season with Reese McGuire as their second catcher, the Sox cut him and called up Romo, who has earned the trust of pitchers and coaches.</p><p>“He commands the game so well,” said left-hander Anthony Kay, who threw six innings of two-run ball in the victory Saturday against the Guardians with Romo behind the plate. “You see the work that he puts in pregame. The communication in between innings also is massive. If you want him to do something different, he listens and he picks it up right away. Having open communication both ways is what builds that relationship and trust.”</p><p>Speaking of Saturday, Sox bench coach Walker McKinven, who doubles as the catchers coach, said Romo arguably had one of the best defensive games a Sox player has had all season.</p><p>“He had a very, very positive receiving game,” McKinven said. “He made that great play on the safety squeeze; he threw a runner out. Really sneaky huge game, despite what happened on the other side of the baseball. I credit Drew a lot for us winning. He handled Anthony well. He made adjustments when necessary. Anything he sees and adjusts on the fly is because he’s well-prepared.”</p><p>That work is keeping Romo with the Sox, perhaps even into the playoffs, where pitching and defense can carry the day.</p><p>“Measurably, he does well in things that we value, and that’s really propping up his aggregate value,” McKinven said. “He works really hard on his receiving, his throwing, his preparing for baserunning from the opposition. Just really a well-prepared dude, prideful dude about the position, which is required at that position. He’s a great teammate, and that goes a long way as a catcher earning people’s trust.”</p><p>Fans often can see a Sox pitcher, such as Kay on Saturday, emphatically point toward Romo and vice versa after a strikeout. But Romo is still working on certain aspects of catching, such as framing.</p><p>“The run value with framing is most important,” he said. “And also my throwing; I’ve had some errors recently. So making sure I’m in the right position to make an accurate throw, work on throwing from different positions.”</p><p>Romo is still working on his hitting, too. Since hitting five home runs and posting an .857 OPS in his first 17 games, he has zero homers and a .252 OPS in his last 30.</p><p>“We’ve been working on so many good things,” Romo said. “Everything that we work on in the cage and in practice is great. And then in the game, it just hasn’t clicked, and it’s super weird. But I’m glad that I’ve been able to contribute on defense. That’s my contribution to this team; that’s how I help the team win games. So I’m proud of that.”</p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-show-loadmore="true" ><a class="AnchorLink" entries.title: Bears Training Camp Report, Day 12: RB D'Andre Swift shines in scrimmage
entries.summary: <p>Breaking down the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" >Bears’ </a>Tuesday training camp practice:<br> </p><h3><b>What happened</b></h3><p>Despite Ben Johnson predicting a “big-time practice,” the Bears’ long-awaited scrimmage wasn’t nearly as blood-thirsty as the physical session the team held at this time last year. The plays weren’t scripted, the atmosphere was controlled and practice ended earlier than the original schedule dictated.</p><p>The Bears’ first-team offense went against the first-team and second-team defense, and vice versa.</p><p>Two running backs stood out at practice — for different reasons. D’Andre Swift rattled off a 62-yard touchdown down the right sideline against the second-team defense. Later, Roschon Johnson fumbled at his own 1-yard line when hit by cornerback Dontae Manning. Veteran linebacker Jon Rhattigan recovered the ball for a touchdown.</p><p>Earlier, when the first-team offense started at their own 1, Rome Odunze caught a pass and ran 58 yards to flip the field.</p><p>Practice ended after safety Skyler Thomas intercepted Tyson Bagent in a two-minute drill.</p><h3><b>Injury update</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Bears players who didn’t participate include receivers Luther Burden and Zavion Thomas; cornerbacks Jaylon Jones and Terell Smith; left tackle Braxton Jones; linebacker D’Marco Jackson; guard Luke Newman; and defensive end Montez Sweat.</p><p>Linebacker Tony Fields II left practice early and rode back on a cart. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson wasn't spotted in the final team drill.</p><h3><b>What’s next?</b></h3><p>The Bears are off Wednesday before returning to practice Thursday at Halas entries.title: Simple seasonings are key in grilled whole beef tenderloin
entries.summary: <p>We love the lively heat and distinctive smokiness from cooking over a bed of glowing red and white-hot coals any time of the year, which is why we have a whole chapter on grilling in our cookbook “Canal House: Cook Something: Recipes to Rely On.”</p><p>We are partial to charcoal grilling in a kettle grill, but if we are short on time or feeling a little lazy, we'll fire up the gas barbie (less fun, less flavor, but more controllable). Either way we follow a few basic tenets when we get our grill on.</p><p>Stick by the grill and pay close attention. Flare-ups happen fast, and the black carbon coating from grilling directly over fire tastes acrid. Tame unwanted flames not with a water spray bottle, but by moving the food to a cooler spot on the grill, or by taking it off the grill until the coals quiet down. Resist fussing with food on the grill until grill marks are well established; this helps reduce sticking. Grilling well requires making friends with fire and being a good companion.</p><p>When we're grilling a hunk of meat, we usually keep the seasonings quite simple to begin, then slather on some flavorful compound butter at the end.</p><h3>Grilled Whole Beef Tenderloin</h3><p>Serves 12</p><p><b>Ingredients</b></p><p><b>Compound Herb Butter</b></p><p>½ pound (2 sticks) room-temperature salted butter<br>½ cup chopped fresh herbs (one or a combination of your favorite herbs)<br>1 small finely chopped shallot or trimmed scallion<br>1 minced garlic clove<br>Salt<br>Freshly ground black pepper</p><p>Grilled Tenderloin</p><p>1 whole beef tenderloin, 6 to 7 pounds<br>1 to 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil<br>2 to 3 tablespoons coarsely ground black pepper<br>Salt</p><p>Directions</p><p>Beat the butter in a medium bowl with a wooden spoon until smooth and creamy. Add the herbs, chopped shallot or scallion, and minced garlic. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper, and stir until well combined. You should have about 1 cup of herb butter.</p><p>Pat the tenderloin dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, trim off any fat. Slide the blade under the long silvery membrane, trimming it off. Fold under about 6 inches of the thin end of the meat, which should make it about as thick as the rest of the filet so it will cook evenly. Tie the tenderloin into a neat package with kitchen string, then rub it all over with oil. Rub with pepper, pressing it into the meat, and season with salt.</p><p>Prepare a medium-hot charcoal or gas grill. Grill the filet over the hottest part of the grill, turning it once a brown and charry crust develops. Brown all over, then move it to a cooler spot on the grill to finish cooking until the internal temperature reaches 120°F for rare and 130°F for medium-rare. Grilling time will vary depending on your grill and the heat. Start checking the internal temperature after 20 minutes.</p><p>Let the tenderloin rest on a cutting board for 15 minutes. Snip off the string, slice the meat and serve warm with a smear of Compound Herb Butter. Or let it cool, wrap and refrigerate for up to 3 days before serving it cold and sliced.<br>___</p><p><i>Melissa Hamilton is a food stylist and cofounder of Canal House. She previously worked at Saveur as the test kitchen director and food editor, and worked in the kitchens of Martha Stewart Living and Cook's Illustrated. She was the cofounder and first executive chef of Hamilton's Grill Room in Lambertville, New Jersey.</i></p><p><i>Christopher Hirsheimer is an award-winning photographer and cofounder of Canal House. Her experience includes establishing a publishing venture, running a culinary and design studio, and publishing an annual series of three seasonal cookbooks titled Canal House Cooking.</i><br>___</p><p>Excerpted from "Canal House: Cook Something" by Christopher Hirsheimer & Melissa Hamilton. Used with permission of Voracious, an imprint of Little, Brown and Company. New York, NY. All rights reserved.</p>

entries.title: Black sesame and miso put an Asian spin on Rice Krispie treats
entries.summary: <p>I make these Black Sesame-Brown Butter Rice Krispies Treats, excerpted from my book "108 Asian Cookies," with my mother in mind.</p><p>Growing up, I ate my fair share of Rice Krispie Treats because they were one of the few Western sweets my mom made over and over again. Maybe it was because they were so easy to make and helped her feel a little closer to the typical mothers we saw on American sitcoms and primetime TV. Or maybe she just liked their chewiness.</p><p>But for whatever reason, my mom never gave her Rice Krispies Treats an Asian spin. She always followed the recipe directions on the cereal box to a T.</p><p>But she loves black sesame desserts, especially sweet black sesame soup. As a child, I remember her telling me how black sesame would keep our Chinese hair black and long. We both have short hair peppered with gray now, but we still have a thing for desserts that sport a lovely shade of gray or black.</p><h3>Black Sesame and Brown Butter Rice Krispie Treats</h3><p>Servings: 12 to 16 Rice Krispie Treats<br>Prep and cook time: 55 minutes</p><p><b>Ingredients</b></p><p>6 tablespoons unsalted butter<br>One 12-ounce bag mini marshmallows<br>1/4 cup black sesame seeds<br>2 1/2 tablespoons black sesame paste<br>1 teaspoon red miso<br>6 cups Rice Krispies cereal<br>1/3 cup freeze-dried strawberry slices or haw flakes (optional)</p><p><b>Directions</b></p><p>Crumple, then uncrumple a large sheet of parchment paper and use it to line a 9-inch-square cake pan with some overhang. Smooth and press down the parchment paper with your hands. Alternatively, generously grease the baking dish with butter or toasted sesame oil.</p><p>To make the brown butter, melt the butter in a heavy saucepan or pot over medium heat while whisking continuously until the butter foams, the foam subsides, the butter is golden, and brown (not black) bits form on the bottom, at least 5 minutes. You're looking for a nutty aroma and not a burnt smell. Reduce the heat to low and add the marshmallows. Stir until the marshmallows have melted into one thick fluff, like foamy, melty mozzarella cheese, a few minutes. There should be no lumps of marshmallow. Add the black sesame seeds, black sesame paste, and miso and mix to combine. Turn off the heat and dump in the cereal, about 2 cups at a time, while stirring; if you like, add the freeze-dried strawberries or haw flakes as well. Stir and mix with a spatula or wooden spoon until all the ingredients are thoroughly coated with gray-black melted marshmallows.</p><p>Transfer the mixture to the prepared pan and flatten into a leveled square. I find it easier to do this with a layer of parchment paper on top and pressing down with a fondant smoother. You can also use a greased spatula or your clean hands when the mixture is cool enough to touch.</p><p>Cover and let it rest on the counter at room temperature for about 30 minutes to let the mixture set. Then, use a sharp knife to cut into 12 to 16 equal pieces.<br>___</p><p><i>Kat Lieu is a food writer, recipe developer, content creator and founder of the popular online group Subtle Asian Baking, which aims to spread the love of Asian baking and fundraises for Asian American and Native Hawaiian-Pacific Islander communities. She lives in Renton, Washington.</i></p><p><i>Excerpted from "108 Asian Cookies" by Kat Lieu. Copyright (copyright) 2025 by Kathleen Lieu. Used with permission of Voracious, an imprint of Little, Brown and Company. New York, NY. All rights reserved.</i><br></p>

entries.title: Dion Jackson, radio personality and booster of Chicago hip-hop talent, dies at 51
entries.summary: <p></p><p></p><p></p><p>A few weeks after Dion Jackson was born, the sleeping infant was on his mother's bed when she left for a moment to run to the bathroom.</p><p>When she returned, the baby was dangling from the side of the bed, gripping the sheets with both hands.</p><p>"He was holding on for dear life, and for me to see that, how tight he was holding on, I knew he was going to be something," said his mother, Connie Jackson.</p><p>Similar derring-do was on display a few decades later when Mr. Jackson, then known as Chicago radio personality "Spank Boogie," went out on a limb.</p><p>Mr. Jackson locked himself in the studio of WGCI-FM (107.5) and went against the wishes of his bosses who wanted him to play trending music.</p><p>He instead played tracks from a series of Chicago rap artists who hadn't established a name for themselves. He was fired for the stunt.</p><p>"Spank felt Chicago music didn't get the type of exposure it deserved," said former WGCI colleague Shannon "Trey the Choklit Jock" Brazier. "He gained respect from Chicago hip-hop artists for that stunt he pulled."</p><p>His four-hour hip-hop show "Boogie Nights" started at 10 p.m. and aired on WGCI in the late '90s and early 2000s, until his stunt.</p><p>"He opened the door for a lot of young Chicago talent to be recognized through the power of radio," said his sister Connie Faye Jackson.</p><p>Mr. Jackson was known to Chicago listeners for shouting a promotional tagline for the clothing store Belvidere Blues with a spirited "Belvidere Blues, baby!"</p><p>He also worked at several other local radio stations and regularly hosted night club dance parties in Chicago featuring top deejays.</p><p>Mr. Jackson died July 24 in Los Angeles from natural causes, family said. He was 51.</p><p>After getting his career off the ground in Chicago, he did radio stints in Wisconsin, Michigan, Connecticut and Alaska.</p><p>"When he told our family he was going to Anchorage to be on the radio it was like, 'What? Who goes to Alaska?' He was like a unicorn there, the only person of color, but he was well received and loved it there," his sister said.</p><p>One game Mr. Jackson played on-air was the "don't say um game," in which he'd ask a caller to name, for instance, five different types of soda pop in 10 seconds without saying "um."</p><p>On a whim nearly two decades ago, Mr. Jackson, who grew up in several spots on the South Side, moved to Los Angeles to try to make it as an actor and rapper.</p><p>He made minor appearances on a number of shows like "Two Broke Girls" and "Key and Peele" and also worked in audio engineering.</p><p>In grade school he was a bright student who filled classroom boredom with highjinks, leaving his parents wondering: "What do we do with him? He's getting all A's."</p><p>At 16 he graduated from Whitney Young Magnet High School, where he played trumpet and was on the chess team. </p><p>"I didn't want him to go to college so young, but he was saying 'Mom, I need to go,'" his mother recalled.</p><p>He became a baby-faced freshman at Northern Illinois University who quickly ingratiated himself with classmates by cutting hair in his dorm room and hosting rap battles, occasionally with future actor Wood Harris, who starred in HBO's "The Wire."</p><p>Mr. Jackson, who picked up the nickname Spanky in college, went by the rap handle Spank the Mad Hatter. Harris went by Fruit of the Mind, according to Mr. Jackson's college roommate and longtime friend, Stephen Smith.</p><p>In recent years Mr. Jackson used the stage name Buda Quan.</p><p>Connie Jackson, a chef, accompanied her brother to Los Angeles, where the siblings chased their dreams.</p><p>"We had a hotplate and a skillet and stayed in a hotel for two weeks when we got there, and the drawer under the television became our bread and condiment pantry," she said with a laugh.</p><p>"Spank was one of the coolest people you could ever know, a vibe you wanted to be around, and just a really talented guy with a smile and laugh that were contagious," said former WGCI colleague Jeanne Sparrow.</p><p>A memorial service will be held from 1 to 4 p.m. Aug. 22 at Cornerstone Church, 3440 178th St., in Lansing.</p>

entries.title: Ex-Mets Clay Holmes, David Peterson reunite with eyes on rediscovering best selves, aiding Cubs’ playoff push
entries.summary: <p>WASHINGTON — David Peterson and Clay Holmes left the Mets at relative personal down points.</p><p>Peterson was an All-Star last season but saw his fortunes dip in the second half last season before struggling earlier this year.</p><p>Holmes was great in his first campaign as a big league starter in 2025, even better this season before getting sidelined with a fractured fibula in mid May.</p><p>Neither is a Met anymore, both traded to the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>, where they’re looking to rediscover the best versions of themselves to help power a playoff run.</p><p>“Last year, we talked a lot,” Peterson said of Holmes. “We were next to each other in the clubhouse, so we were always bouncing things off [each other]. … It’s fun to talk the game with him.”</p><p>“It’s good to have a familiar face around,” Holmes said of Peterson. “He’s a guy that, similar to me, has a dry, fun way about him, so we kind of connect on that a little bit. … He’s just a pro. Having guys like that around that are pros, you can trust those guys.”</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/28/cubs-david-peterson-mlb-trade-deadline-mets-jed-hoyer-pitching-staff-rotation-craig-counsell-ground-ball-rate" >Peterson has thrived</a> since coming over in late June, when the Cubs were buried by pitching injuries, needing someone, anyone, to make starts.</p><p>But he’s been more than a fill-in, looking like a reliable playoff option, should the Cubs include him as part of a postseason rotation. He’s thrilled to use his skill in coaxing grounders with a Gold Glove defense behind him.</p><p>Peterson’s 4.03 ERA as a Cub isn’t too exciting, but he’s been excellent in six of his seven starts. Exclude a 10-run clunker against the Cardinals, and his ERA in the other six outings is a microscopic 1.83.</p><p>“I got to see Petey last year, when he was probably at his best,” Holmes said. “He has a way of getting the ball on the ground. It’s fun to see him get back to that. … I’m just excited that he looks like he’s back to where he needs to be.</p><p>“He’s a very versatile guy: a really good starter that can be used in a lot of different ways. When he’s throwing the ball well, it’s a guy you want on the mound.”</p><p>With Peterson’s October role potentially up in the air, versatility isn’t a bad thing. With his history as an All-Star reliever, Holmes has it, too. But while the playoffs can bring anything, he was acquired to be a top-of-the-rotation arm.</p><p>Holmes looked rusty in his first major league start since that May leg injury, allowing four runs in four innings. A briefer outing wasn’t unexpected, but the Cubs will certainly expect more once he’s got his sea legs back, having parted with No. 2 prospect Jefferson Rojas <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-trade-deadline-clay-holmes-mets" >to land him and outfielder Tyrone Taylor</a>.</p><p>“Those are two of the best guys that you could ask for,” Peterson said.</p><p>That best version of Holmes is certainly in there. He returned to starting with the Mets last season, posting a 3.53 ERA in 33 outings. He had a 2.39 ERA in nine starts this year before hitting the IL.</p><p>Holmes, too, figures to benefit from <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/06/cubs-defense-mlb-trade-deadline-kevin-gausman-clay-holmes-gold-gloves-pitching-injuries-braxton-garrett" >the Cubs’ dazzling defense</a>, fitting a similar bill to Peterson as a ground-ball generator. If they get the version of Holmes the Mets did, he’ll shoot right to the top of that playoff starting staff.</p><p>“You’re going to get a guy that goes out there and gives you a chance to win,” Peterson said, “just another guy that knows how to go through a lineup multiple times, has all the weapons and pitches to be super successful. He’s shown that. It’s more firepower for us.”</p><p>With both guys in the fold, a pitching staff that suffered from depth issues earlier this summer — and last fall — is looking capable of helping, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/09/cubs-matthew-boyd-starting-rotation-kevin-gausman-clay-holmes-colin-rea-pitching-staff-playoffs" >perhaps powering</a>, the Cubs toward their No. 1 goal.</p><p>“It’s a group that can elevate each other, and it doesn’t have to be the same guy every night,” Peterson said. “When you have a group where everyone’s pulling the rope in the same direction, it makes us stronger as a unit and a harder team to beat.”</p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" entries.title: Potential class-action lawsuit filed against South Deering funeral home for mishandling 56 bodies
entries.summary: <p>A Texas woman launched a potential class-action lawsuit Tuesday against the South Deering funeral home that allegedly mishandled the remains of her father along with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/08/06/decomposing-bodies-found-funeral-home-south-chicago-chapel-95th-street" target="_blank" ><u>dozens of other bodies</u></a> that were found in various states of unrefrigerated decomposition last week.</p><p>South Chicago Chapel took possession of Terrance Fallie’s body the day he died Aug. 4, according to the suit filed in Cook County Circuit Court by his daughter, Dyanna Burt-Finnie.</p><p>That was four days after the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation first received “information about potential operational concerns” at the facility run by <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago/2026/08/07/owners-of-far-south-side-funeral-home-have-history-of-mishandling-human-remains" target="_blank" ><u>Clark and Johanna Morgan</u></a><u>.</u> Johanna Morgan's state funeral director license was suspended Aug. 5 for allowing “decedents to be kept in an unrefrigerated area with deplorable conditions.”</p><p>Representatives for Burt-Finnie went to the chapel at 2939 E. 95th St. on Aug. 6 to take Fallie’s body to another funeral home, arriving as <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/08/10/south-chicago-chapel-funeral-home-oversight-illinois-decomposing-bodies" target="_blank" ><u>city, county and state authorities</u></a> were removing 56 bodies that had been neglected, according to officials and the suit.</p><p>Burt-Finnie’s suit notes “neighbors had smelled an odor akin to a dead animal emanating from Defendant’s funeral home for approximately two months prior to the discovery.”</p><p>The grisly conditions were revealed a year after the state shut down <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2025/06/19/chicago-heights-crematory-bodies-death-license-closed" target="_blank" ><u>a Chicago Heights crematory</u></a> run by the Morgans, who are facing more than 20 lawsuits for allegedly mishandling the remains of about 100 people in that case.</p><p>An attorney representing the Morgans did not respond to requests for comment.</p><p>Clark Morgan lost his funeral director’s license for “unprofessional conduct” and working on an expired license in 2024, state records show.</p><p>Criminal charges haven’t been filed. Illinois State Police are still investigating the Chicago Heights situation while Chicago police sort through the latest ordeal. The Cook County medical examiner’s office is still working to identify all the deceased as well as the cremated remains of at least 56 more people.</p><p>South Chicago Chapel “failed to properly affix identifying information to the bodies in its possession, including that of Mr. Fallie, despite knowing the same would be necessary in properly identifying the bodies,” the new suit claims.</p><p>The six-count suit alleges South Chicago Chapel interfered with families’ right to possess remains; inflicted emotional distress; violated state law on the disposition of remains; committed fraud; and misrepresented their business.</p><p>An initial hearing was scheduled for Oct. 13.</p>
entries.author: Mitchell Armentrout

entries.title: Mayor Johnson names as his new CFO a senior director from Fitch Ratings
entries.summary: <p>Under pressure to stabilize his finance team before an investors conference and a preelection budget battle, Mayor Brandon Johnson has chosen a senior director at Fitch Ratings to serve as his new chief financial officer.</p><p>Ashlee Gabrysch replaces Steven Mahr, who abruptly resigned, along with his top deputy, just days before veteran Budget Director Annette Guzman followed both men out the door.</p><p>Gabrysch currently serves as senior director and mid-central region manager at Fitch Ratings. Since 2019, she has served as Fitch's lead analyst for both Chicago and Illinois.</p><p>That makes the new CFO familiar with the city’s $36 billion pension crisis and the marathon budget battle that saw a City Council majority reject Johnson’s corporate head tax and pass an alternative city budget. The spending plan, includes revenues the mayor continues to oppose — and that have fallen short of projections.</p><p>That has left the city with a $90 million mid-year shortfall. As a result, Mahr and Guzman raised the prospect of employee layoffs and pulled back on their commitment to make the second half of a $260 million advance pension payment at the center of the budget battle.</p><p>Civic Federation President Joe Ferguson said “somebody with the right credentials could make a difference,” and Gabrysch fills the bill.</p><p>“What nobody can really know is how she will handle… what is likely to be the resistance to, let’s call it more conventional, mainstream guidance on critical financing issues for the city,” Ferguson said.</p><div class="Enhancement" </div><p>As Fitch's Chicago analyst, Gabrysch knows that the full pension advance is “one of those anchors” that investors and Wall Street rating agencies “have looked at for stabilization purposes,” Ferguson said.</p><p></p><p>Ferguson predicted that there will be “direct questioning” about the pension advance at the investors conference and that Gabrysch’s responses will be “very telling.”</p><p>“She knows exactly the importance of these signals and knows exactly how they factor into rating agency considerations, and market considerations as well,” Ferguson said.</p><p>Justin Marlowe, director for the Center for Municipal Finance at the University of Chicago, called Gabrysch a “stabilizing pick” because she is a “known commodity to bond investors” with a “strong view… about the need to make the full advance pension payment.”</p><p>“Knowing Ashlee, I think it will not only be, `You need to make the second half of the payment,’ [but], `Let me help you find a path toward finding the money to do that,’“ Marlowe told the Sun-Times.</p><p>“Whether the mayor takes that advice is a separate question, of course. But she has made very clear that the advance pension payments have been a real important part of stabilizing the city’s credit quality over the last few years, and that the market will see not making that payment as not only a pause in progress, but potentially backsliding.”</p><p>Gabrysch could not be reached for comment.</p><p>A City Hall news release quoted her as saying she is “honored… to serve the city that has shaped my professional career in public finance.”</p><p>“I have spent more than a decade studying and working on the fiscal issues facing Chicago and Illinois, both inside government and from the perspective of the municipal markets,” Gabrysch said. “I know the seriousness of the challenges before us, but I also know the strength and resilience of this city. I look forward to bringing my experience, analytical rigor and commitment to public service” to the job and working with the City Council and others to “build a stronger and more sustainable financial future.”</p><p>The rapid-fire resignations of Mahr, his top deputy and Guzman have raised serious questions about financial instability, largely because of the timing of those departures and the enormity of the city’s fiscal problems.</p><p>Mahr replaced Jill Jaworski, who left City Hall in January for a job at Navy Pier shortly after a City Council majority rejected Johnson’s corporate head tax and muscled through an alternative city budget. </p><p>Chicago faces a $90 million mid-year shortfall, a $1 billion budget gap next year and a $36 billion pension crisis that has two of four city employee pension funds hovering dangerously close to insolvency — even after receiving a city loan to avoid selling assets to pay liabilities.</p><p>The city is weeks away from a grueling election-year budget season, and days away from an investors conference. Johnson has tried to ease concerns about the high-level turnover by claiming that, so long as he is the mayor, Chicago has all of the stability it needs.</p>
